per_window.ps-ns: dynamic_in_window at the termini with an ordered core. Free CXCL8(1-66) at 25 °C, pH 6.0 phosphate, 100 µM: low S2 at E4-R6 and seven model-5 sites (S2 about 0.55, tau_s 0.5-3.5 ns) (CXCL8-J1, r13); other residues S2 0.80-0.87 (J2). At pH 7.3 HEPES, 40 and 15 °C: negative NOE for A2-R6, NOE about 0.8 for C7-F65 (J3, J4; r34, r35). Receptor-peptide binding raises most S2 (J16). Full-length dimer (J21, J22) and the monomer-biased L25Y/V27R mutant (J27) also have mobile termini.
per_window.us-ms: dynamic_in_window at two sites, no rate. Free 1-66 monomer, 25 °C, pH 6.0, 600/800 MHz CPMG: K23 (800 MHz only, fast-limit fit) and V62 (slow-limit fit) disperse (J7, r15); I10, S14, E63 and all other amides are flat although model-free Rex exceeded 1 s-1 at I10, S14, E63 (J8). Bound to the CXCR1 N-domain peptide, T12, Y13, S14, V41, E48, C50 exchange with kex 900-2000 s-1 and a 1-2% minor state (J12, r16), F17 is flat (J13), K15 and V58 are too weak to fit (J14). Peptide binding kinetics koff 2400-6500 s-1 (J15) are binding, not conformational. The full-length dimer has H(S/M)QC exchange near R26 and C50 with flat 600 MHz CPMG (J23, J24). Mutant and high-concentration dispersion is self-association (J9, J28).
per_window.slower_than_ms: search_insufficient (J41). Only a one-hour D2O snapshot with five unnamed protected beta-sheet amides exists (J10, unresolved).
per_window.undetermined: Free 1-66: N-terminal RDCs near zero (J5, indirect), missing S1 and L66 (J6), construct-dependent N-loop and F65 position versus the dimer (J11). Bound states: receptor-fragment peak loss at K15, D52, V58 (J17), tighter complex ensemble (J18), Site-I to Site-II contact switching in one 800 ns MD (J19), Fab crystal (J20), receptor cryo-EM (J36), SpyCEP (J35). Oligomer and GAG: dimer tumbling with peptide (J25, J29), restrained MD of dimer versus mutant (J26, J30), CS binding (J31-J34), native MS 18:82 monomer:dimer (J37), antibody SPR (J38). Abstract-only structural and partner papers (J39, J40).

protein_summary.wt_apo_answer: Yes, at two sites without rate or population: the free entry construct CXCL8(1-66) at 100 µM (>99% monomer), 25 °C, pH 6.0 in 50 mM sodium phosphate shows 15N CPMG dispersion only at K23 (800 MHz only, fast-limit fit) and V62 (C-terminal helix, slow-limit fit), with all other observed amides flat; the authors print no kex, population or shift difference.
open_conflicts: Model-free Rex above 1 s-1 at I10, S14 and E63 (r13) is not confirmed by CPMG on the same sample, which disperses only at K23 and V62 (r15); the authors attribute small Rex to tumbling anisotropy or fitting.

Full-length dimer: H(S/M)QC shift differences report exchange at R26 and C50 (r5) while 600 MHz CPMG is flat (r6); the authors reconcile this by placing the process in the microsecond range, which no row measures.
questions_for_gina: Is the RelaxDB CXCL8 set the 2018 free 1-66 monomer data (100 µM, 25 °C, pH 6.0 phosphate, 600 and 800 MHz; doi:10.3390/molecules23112825)? The input card has no BMRB id.
Should the single-residue slow-limit CPMG fit at V62 (AICc-selected, no rate or population printed) count as an alternate-APO candidate, or does that need a fitted kex and pB?
protein_summary.buffer_note: The entry construct is the C-terminally truncated CXCL8(1-66), a monomer at the 100 µM relaxation concentration (KM-D about 20 mM) but partly dimeric at 900 µM (J9); full-length 1-72 is a dimer at NMR concentrations, so its rows are other-construct evidence and dimer/monomer exchange is never counted as intramolecular dynamics. The 2018 relaxation and CPMG data are in 50 mM sodium phosphate pH 6.0 and the lineshape titration at 30 °C; no phosphate artefact is shown, but GAG and receptor binding are electrostatic and buffer-sensitive. The 2017 1-66 data are in 20 mM HEPES pH 7.3 at 40 and 15 °C. The 2014 paper's I11 and A15 labels do not match the sequence (K11, K15) and are left unmapped. The second read raised no flags for this case.
